clue.text: Liquid food that'll make you very high

parts.note: so is an intensifier meaning very, as in 'so tired'
up means high, as in prices being up

explanation.surface: A warning about some potent broth that will send its eater soaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is a dish served as a liquid, often as a starter course.

clue.text: Old friend gets precious stone

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A former companion is presented with a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: The opal is an iridescent gemstone prized in jewellery.

clue.text: Workers in a National Trust site, initially?

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Asks whether insects are busy at a heritage property.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants are the sterile females that forage and build, so ants are classic crossword workers.

clue.text: Fruit covering back of head? It's a neckerchief!

indicators.note: covering means the fruit wraps around the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a banana is a fruit

indicators.note: back of asks for the final letter of the word head

explanation.surface: A joke about wrapping a banana skin round the back of your head and calling it a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts D, the last letter of 'head', inside BANANA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandana is a square of cloth tied round the neck or head, a type of kerchief.

clue.text: Police on outskirts of Stranraer disturbed to find burial site

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged
outskirts are the edges of a town, so this takes the first and last letters of Stranraer

explanation.surface: Officers in a Scottish town are shaken to discover a graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: Stranraer is a port town in south-west Scotland; its outer letters give SR, mixed with POLICE and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A necropolis, literally a city of the dead, is a large ancient cemetery.

clue.text: Firm friend admits writing articles to make amends

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the friend's letters take the other piece inside them

parts.note: a mate is a friend
pens are articles used for writing

explanation.surface: A company colleague confesses to writing pieces in order to make up for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests A, AN or THE; here 'writing articles' is simply PENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To compensate is to make up for a loss or wrong, which is what making amends means.

clue.text: Yes, a rich criminal will fence a piece of furniture

indicators.note: to fence is to enclose, so the jumbled letters surround the single letter
criminal means crooked or wrong, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A wealthy crook agrees to handle stolen furniture, fence being slang for a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' looks like the receiver of stolen goods, which suits 'criminal'; here it means enclose, so the second A goes inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large comfortable armchair, one item of furniture.

clue.text: Woman has time to get ingredient for dumplings

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman finds a moment to fetch something for her dumpling recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet, hard animal fat, is the traditional fat in British dumplings and puddings.

clue.text: Moving awkwardly, displaying fake jewellery

parts.note: sham means fake or counterfeit
bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone lurching along while wearing costume jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: To shamble is to walk with a clumsy, shuffling gait, so shambling is moving that way.

clue.text: Royal helpers, we're told, making barriers

indicators.note: we're told means the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: palace aides are the helpers of a royal household

explanation.surface: Servants at court are reportedly putting up fences.
explanation.definitionFit: Palisades are fences of pointed stakes built as defences, a kind of barrier.

clue.text: One member that's a mischievous type

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A single member of a group turns out to be a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a small devil, and by extension a naughty child.

clue.text: Distinctive quality of a posh artist

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class usage, hence posh
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Something special about an upper-class painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the special atmosphere or character that surrounds a person or place.

clue.text: Send back part of spring vegetable

indicators.note: send back says the month is written backwards

parts.note: May is a month that forms part of spring

explanation.surface: Returning some of the spring produce from the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests a coil or a well; here it is the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The yam is a starchy tuber eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Musical on my ship arranged by Charlie

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, as music is arranged

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie puts on a stage show aboard his vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Symphonic describes music of a symphony, so it is a grand sense of musical.

clue.text: Biscuit or loaf that doesn't reach the edge of a baking tin?

definitions.text: loaf that doesn't reach the edge of a baking tin?
definitions.meaning: a loaf that falls short of the tin's edge is, read literally

explanation.surface: A baker's puzzle about a cake or a loaf that has not risen to fill its tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a rich crumbly biscuit; 'short' in baking means crumbly with fat.

clue.text: Coat that's made by Apple

definitions.meaning: a ..., also spelt mackintosh, is a waterproof raincoat
the line of computers made by Apple

explanation.surface: A garment produced by the technology company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple' also suggests the fruit, and McIntosh is an apple variety, but here it is the computer maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The raincoat is named after Charles Macintosh; Apple named its computer after the apple variety.

clue.text: Take charge of company making bedroom furniture?

parts.note: to head something is to lead or take charge of it
a board is the body of directors that runs a company

explanation.surface: Someone running a firm that makes beds and wardrobes.
explanation.definitionFit: A headboard is the upright panel at the head of a bed, part of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: Rolls seen coming back from Vespa building

indicators.note: coming back says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Rolls-Royce spotted returning from a scooter factory.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Rolls seen' as the definition; 'seen' is only a link, and 'from' signals the hidden letters. Vespa is an Italian scooter brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Baps are soft bread rolls, a British word.

clue.text: Study exotic lace mask

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters are made unfamiliar by rearranging

explanation.surface: Examining a foreign lace face covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To mask something is to hide it, the same as to conceal it.

clue.text: Graduate with cold in a bad way — I could get germs!

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ill means unwell, in a bad way

explanation.surface: A student with a chill fears catching bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, popularly called germs.

clue.text: Greed: a sin ensnaring a king

indicators.note: ensnaring means trapping, so the sin holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a vice is a sin
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A statement that greed is one sin that can trap even a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Heads turning in shock

indicators.note: turning means turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: nut is slang for head, so heads are nuts

explanation.surface: People's heads swivel in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or shock someone.

clue.text: Live with means, perhaps — though not started — to make drinks?

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live

indicators.note: not started means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: averages are an example of means in statistics, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Advice to live within one's means, with drinks somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' suggests money; here it is the statistical mean, an average.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water.

clue.text: A point that's highly relevant

explanation.surface: A remark that is very much to the purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt describes something suitable and pertinent to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Pair captured by Catwoman

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A couple of crooks caught by the comic-book villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a pair is a couple, the number of items in a matched set like gloves.

clue.text: So, after sign of hesitation, proceed

indicators.note: after places the word for proceed following the hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound people make when they hesitate
to go is to proceed

explanation.surface: Someone pauses, then decides to carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to mean so.

clue.text: Striking a Republican on a break?

parts.note: someone on a break is resting

explanation.surface: Asks whether a politician taking time off counts as industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like a walkout, which 'on a break' supports; it means eye-catching.
explanation.definitionFit: Arresting means striking in the sense of catching the attention.

clue.text: Second drink is a bargain

parts.note: a nip is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: Having another tot of whisky is good value.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is British informal for something cheap, a bargain.

clue.text: Island in fashion again

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A holiday isle is trendy once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fashion' reads as one phrase meaning trendy; 'in' is the signal and the letters straddle fashion and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Tease about black clothes

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: Mocking someone's dark outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothing, especially of a distinctive kind.

clue.text: Rush just a little bit

definitions.meaning: a small amount, as of milk

explanation.definitionFit: Dash means both a quick sprint and a small splash added to something.

clue.text: One looks for meaning in this

definitions.text: One looks for meaning in this

parts.words: One looks for meaning in this
parts.note: the book you consult to find what words mean

explanation.surface: Sounds like a search for life's purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference book lists words with their senses, so people consult it to learn definitions.
